mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 5.33% is above the 5.0% threshold, which historically predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.0% within a 3-month window, it signals labor market deterioration that increases equity risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5.0% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 305.0, it signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that increases equity risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0 and CPIAUCSL > 305.0

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by UNRATE < 4.0% and HOUST > 1300.0), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and rising interest rates, leading to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and HOUST > 1300.0

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 in a 3-month window, it signals a weakening economy that increases equity risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0

failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS > 700000.0
